seoTitle: How eBay's Authenticity Guarantee Works for Sellers (2026)
metaDescription: Selling sneakers, watches, handbags, jewelry or streetwear on eBay? Authenticity Guarantee is automatic once a listing clears the category's price threshold, not something you switch on. Here's how it actually works.
intro: eBay's Authenticity Guarantee puts eBay's own inspection process behind certain high-value listings, sneakers, handbags, watches, jewelry, and streetwear, and marks qualifying items with a blue checkmark buyers see right in search results. There is no setting to switch on: eBay's own seller documentation states plainly that eligible listings are enrolled automatically, with no opt in or opt out. What decides whether your listing qualifies is category and price, and the threshold is different for every category. This guide covers those thresholds, what happens to the item after a sale, and what the badge changes for a buyer comparing listings.

steps.heading: Understand that this is automatic, not something you turn on
steps.body: eBay's Authenticity Guarantee landing page frames the program in one line, real items, checked by real experts, and notes in the footer that it runs independently of the brands themselves. It is eBay's own authentication service, not a manufacturer partnership. Crucially, eBay's help documentation for sellers states that a qualifying item "will be automatically added to the program, free of charge," with no opt in or opt out option. There is no listing toggle to find. If your item sits in an eligible category and clears that category's price threshold, the program applies on its own.

image.caption: eBay's Authenticity Guarantee landing page: "Real items. Checked by real experts," with a note that the program is independent from, and not associated with, any of the brands sold.

steps.heading: Check your category, its price threshold, and item condition
steps.body:
Each category has its own minimum price, and an item below that line never enters the authentication pipeline no matter how the listing is set up. Several categories also carry a second, lower tier where authentication becomes an optional add-on the buyer can choose to pay for at checkout, rather than an automatic free service, so the same category can behave two different ways depending on price.

Condition matters alongside price. A heavily worn or modified item is more likely to fail inspection after a buyer has already paid, so an accurate, honest description before listing reduces that risk.

image.caption: Authenticity Guarantee's category breakdown, sneakers, handbags, watches, jewelry, and streetwear each link to their own eligibility and process details.

steps.heading: Ship to eBay's authentication facility, not the buyer
steps.body: Once a buyer purchases a qualifying item, it does not go straight to them. eBay's seller pages direct the seller to ship it to an eBay authentication facility inside the United States, generally within the seller's own stated handling time, and several categories provide a free prepaid shipping label for that leg specifically. A specialist in that category inspects the item there before it continues to the buyer. Sending the item by a separate, custom shipping arrangement instead of the one eBay directs risks the parcel never reaching the authenticator.

steps.heading: See the badge appear once your listing qualifies
steps.body: Once a listing meets the program's category and price rules, a blue Authenticity Guarantee checkmark appears directly under the price in search results and on the item page itself, visible before a buyer ever clicks in. This visibility is the mechanism behind the trust boost sellers report: buyers comparing several similar listings can see at a glance which ones carry third-party verification, which counts for more in categories with real counterfeit risk, sneakers and handbags among them.

image.caption: Search results for New Balance sneakers, with an Authenticity Guarantee checkmark shown directly under several listings, buyers see this badge before they ever open the item page.

steps.heading: Know the delivery timeline and how returns work
steps.body:
eBay's help documentation states authentication processing generally finishes within two business days, after which the item ships to the buyer by expedited, signature-confirmed delivery, about two days for most categories. That is one extra shipping leg compared with a direct sale, worth a line in your listing description so a buyer is not surprised by the timing.

If a buyer returns the item, it goes back through the authenticator for re-inspection before a refund is issued and the item is returned to you. That re-authentication step is what makes an Authenticity Guarantee return take longer than an ordinary eBay return.

troubleshooting.problem: The item sits in an eligible category but never gets the checkmark
troubleshooting.cause: It is priced below that category's threshold, or it was listed in a sub-category eBay does not route through authentication, sneakers, for instance, only qualify inside the athletic and kids' shoe categories eBay names.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the price against the table above and confirm the listing sits in the specific eligible sub-category, not just the right department.

troubleshooting.problem: A sold item was shipped straight to the buyer instead of to eBay
troubleshooting.cause: The seller used their own shipping arrangement instead of the label or facility address eBay's program directs for that sale.
troubleshooting.fix: Use the shipping method eBay provides for the order. Several categories issue a free prepaid label specifically for the leg to the authentication facility.

troubleshooting.problem: A return is taking longer than a normal eBay return
troubleshooting.cause: Returned items go through re-authentication before a refund is issued, which is a step ordinary returns do not have.
troubleshooting.fix: This is expected; there is nothing to fix beyond waiting for the re-inspection to clear.

faq.question: Do I need to enroll my listing in Authenticity Guarantee?
faq.answer: No. eBay's own documentation states there is no opt in or opt out; an eligible listing is added to the program automatically once it clears its category's price threshold.

faq.question: What's the minimum price for my item to qualify?
faq.answer: It depends on the category: $75 or more for sneakers, $200 or more for streetwear, $500 or more for handbags and jewelry, and $2,000 or more for watches, per eBay's current category pages.

faq.question: Who pays for the authentication?
faq.answer: eBay covers the cost at the automatic, mandatory threshold in every category. Below that, in handbags, jewelry and watches, a buyer can optionally pay $40 or $80 at checkout to add the same inspection to a lower-priced item; the seller is never charged.

faq.question: How much longer does delivery take with Authenticity Guarantee?
faq.answer: eBay states processing generally finishes within two business days, then the item ships to the buyer by expedited delivery, about two days for most categories, on top of the time it took to reach the authenticator.

faq.question: What happens if a buyer returns an authenticated item?
faq.answer: It goes back through the authenticator for re-inspection before eBay issues the refund and returns the item to the seller.
